topics.label: OSI Model
topics.desc: Seven-layer reference abstraction that decomposes communication into physical, link, network, transport, session, presentation, and application concerns.

topics.label: TCP/IP Model
topics.desc: Four-layer practical stack (link, internet, transport, application) underpinning the real Internet, mapped loosely onto OSI.

topics.label: Encapsulation & PDUs
topics.desc: Each layer wraps the layer above in headers (and sometimes trailers), forming frames, packets, segments, and messages as protocol data units.

topics.label: Layering & Abstraction
topics.desc: Design principle isolating concerns per layer so protocols evolve independently behind stable interfaces, at the cost of some efficiency.

topics.label: End-to-End Principle
topics.desc: Argument that functions like reliability belong at endpoints, keeping the network core simple and pushing intelligence to the edges.

topics.label: Standards & RFCs
topics.desc: IETF RFCs, IEEE 802, and ITU define interoperable protocols through open consensus, with maturity levels from draft to standard.

topics.label: Ethernet
topics.desc: Dominant wired LAN technology (IEEE 802.3) framing data with MAC addresses over twisted-pair or fiber at gigabit-plus speeds.

topics.label: MAC Addressing
topics.desc: 48-bit hardware identifiers assigned per NIC that uniquely address frames within a broadcast domain at the data-link layer.

topics.label: Switching & Bridging
topics.desc: Layer-2 forwarding that learns MAC-to-port mappings to deliver frames only where needed, segmenting collision domains.

topics.label: VLANs & 802.1Q
topics.desc: Logical segmentation of a physical switch into isolated broadcast domains using 802.1Q VLAN tags for traffic separation.

topics.label: ARP
topics.desc: Address Resolution Protocol maps a known IPv4 address to its MAC address on a local segment via broadcast queries.

topics.label: Wi-Fi (802.11)
topics.desc: Wireless LAN standard family using CSMA/CA over shared radio spectrum, with WPA2/WPA3 securing the link.

topics.label: Physical Media & Signaling
topics.desc: Copper, fiber, and radio carrying bits via encoding and modulation, bounded by bandwidth, attenuation, and noise.

topics.label: IPv4 Addressing
topics.desc: 32-bit hierarchical addresses with subnet masks enabling global packet delivery, constrained by exhaustion of the address space.

topics.label: IPv6
topics.desc: 128-bit successor protocol restoring vast address space, with stateless autoconfiguration and simplified headers.

topics.label: Subnetting & CIDR
topics.desc: Classless prefix-length notation that partitions address blocks flexibly and aggregates routes to shrink routing tables.

topics.label: IP Routing & Forwarding
topics.desc: Per-hop longest-prefix-match lookup in routing tables to forward packets toward their destination across networks.

topics.label: NAT & PAT
topics.desc: Network Address Translation rewrites addresses/ports at a boundary, sharing one public IP among many private hosts.

topics.label: Routing Protocols
topics.desc: Distance-vector and link-state algorithms (RIP, OSPF, IS-IS) that distribute reachability to compute intra-domain paths.

topics.label: BGP
topics.desc: Path-vector protocol exchanging routes between autonomous systems, the policy-driven glue holding the global Internet together.

topics.label: ICMP
topics.desc: Control and diagnostic messaging for IP carrying errors, redirects, and echo requests used by ping and traceroute.

topics.label: TCP
topics.desc: Connection-oriented transport providing reliable, ordered, byte-stream delivery via sequence numbers, ACKs, and retransmission.

topics.label: UDP
topics.desc: Connectionless, unreliable datagram transport with minimal overhead, favored for low-latency and real-time traffic.

topics.label: Ports & Sockets
topics.desc: Port numbers multiplex transport connections per host; the 5-tuple plus socket abstraction identifies each endpoint pair.

topics.label: TCP Handshake & Teardown
topics.desc: Three-way SYN/SYN-ACK/ACK setup and four-way FIN teardown establishing and closing reliable connections and their state.

topics.label: Flow Control
topics.desc: Sliding-window mechanism letting a receiver advertise capacity so a fast sender does not overwhelm a slow receiver.

topics.label: Congestion Control
topics.desc: Algorithms like Reno, CUBIC, and BBR that probe and back off to share bottleneck bandwidth and avoid network collapse.

topics.label: QUIC
topics.desc: UDP-based multiplexed transport with built-in TLS, 0-RTT setup, and per-stream loss recovery underpinning HTTP/3.

topics.label: DNS
topics.desc: Hierarchical, distributed name system resolving human-readable domains to IP addresses via recursive and authoritative servers.

topics.label: DNS Records & Zones
topics.desc: Record types (A, AAAA, CNAME, MX, TXT, NS) and delegated zones defining how a domain resolves and is administered.

topics.label: DHCP
topics.desc: Dynamic Host Configuration Protocol leasing IP addresses, gateway, and DNS settings to hosts joining a network.

topics.label: Email Protocols
topics.desc: SMTP for sending plus IMAP/POP3 for retrieval, with MIME, SPF, DKIM, and DMARC layering structure and anti-spoofing.

topics.label: File Transfer Protocols
topics.desc: FTP/FTPS, SFTP, and SCP moving files between hosts, differing in channel model, security, and firewall friendliness.

topics.label: Real-Time Media Protocols
topics.desc: RTP/RTCP, SIP, and WebRTC carrying low-latency audio/video with NAT traversal via STUN/TURN/ICE.

topics.label: WebSockets
topics.desc: Full-duplex persistent channel upgraded from HTTP, enabling low-overhead bidirectional messaging for live applications.

topics.label: HTTP/1.1
topics.desc: Text-based request/response protocol with persistent connections and pipelining, the long-time workhorse of the web.

topics.label: HTTP Methods & Status
topics.desc: Verbs (GET, POST, PUT, DELETE) and status code classes conveying intent and outcome with idempotency and safety semantics.

topics.label: HTTP Headers
topics.desc: Key-value metadata controlling content negotiation, caching, authentication, CORS, and connection behavior per message.

topics.label: HTTP Caching
topics.desc: Cache-Control, ETag, and conditional requests letting clients and proxies reuse responses to cut latency and load.

topics.label: Cookies & Sessions
topics.desc: Stateful tokens stored client-side via Set-Cookie that carry session identity across stateless HTTP requests.

topics.label: HTTP/2
topics.desc: Binary, multiplexed protocol with header compression (HPACK) and server push that eliminates head-of-line blocking at the app layer.

topics.label: HTTP/3
topics.desc: Latest version running over QUIC to remove transport-level head-of-line blocking and speed up connection establishment.

topics.label: TLS / SSL
topics.desc: Transport-layer security providing confidentiality, integrity, and authentication via a handshake negotiating keys and ciphers.

topics.label: PKI & Certificates
topics.desc: X.509 certificates and trusted CA hierarchies binding identities to public keys to authenticate TLS endpoints.

topics.label: Firewalls
topics.desc: Policy enforcement points filtering traffic by address, port, and state, ranging from stateless ACLs to next-gen inspection.

topics.label: VPN & Tunneling
topics.desc: Encrypted tunnels (IPsec, WireGuard, OpenVPN) carrying private traffic securely across untrusted public networks.

topics.label: Network Attacks
topics.desc: Threats like MITM, ARP/DNS spoofing, DDoS, and session hijacking that exploit protocol trust and resource limits.

topics.label: DNSSEC & Encrypted DNS
topics.desc: DNSSEC signs records for authenticity while DoH/DoT encrypt queries to protect resolution integrity and privacy.

topics.label: Socket Programming
topics.desc: The Berkeley socket API (bind, listen, accept, connect, send, recv) for writing networked clients and servers.

topics.label: Packet Capture & Analysis
topics.desc: tcpdump and Wireshark capture and dissect live traffic to inspect headers, flows, and protocol behavior in depth.

topics.label: HTTP Clients & curl
topics.desc: curl, wget, and libraries that craft requests and inspect responses for testing, scripting, and debugging APIs.

topics.label: Diagnostic Tools
topics.desc: ping, traceroute, dig, nslookup, netstat, and ss for probing reachability, paths, name resolution, and open ports.

topics.label: Proxies & Load Balancers
topics.desc: Forward/reverse proxies and L4/L7 load balancers (nginx, HAProxy, Envoy) distributing, terminating, and routing traffic.

topics.label: CDN
topics.desc: Geographically distributed edge caches serving content close to users to cut latency and offload origin servers.
